dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:1201.text: To avoid. Formed from 辵, with 于 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1202.text: To advance or arrive at the furthest point. Formed from 辵, with 𦘔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1203.text: A high, level plain that people ascend. Formed from 辵, 备 and 录. The explanation is incomplete.

shuowen:1204.text: A road on which one travels. Formed from 辵 and 𩠐. A single through route is called 道.

shuowen:1205.text: A relay conveyance. Another explanation: distressed or constrained. Formed from 辵, with 豦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1206.text: An animal's tracks. Formed from 辵, with 亢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1207.text: To arrive. Formed from 辵, with 弔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1208.text: To travel along a hanging cliff. Formed from 辵, with 𦤝 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1209.text: 邂逅: to meet without an appointment. Formed from 辵, with 解 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1210.text: The chance meeting 邂逅. Formed from 辵, with 后 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1211.text: Urgent. Formed from 辵, with 皇 indicating the sound; alternatively formed from 彳.

shuowen:1212.text: Near. Formed from 辵, with 畐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1213.text: Far. Formed from 辵, with 䫉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1214.text: Far. Formed from 辵, with 叚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1215.text: To arrive. Formed from 辵, with 气 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1216.text: To scatter and run. Formed from 辵, with 并 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1217.text: To leap; to pass through. Formed from 辵, with 秀 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1218.text: To patrol. Formed from 辵, with 羅 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1219.text: 迢 means distant, 遰. Formed from 辵, with 召 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1220.text: 逍遥: like soaring freely. Formed from 辵, with 肖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1221.text: The free wandering called 逍遥; also, far. Formed from 辵, with 䍃 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1222.text: Small steps. It depicts the three connected segments of a person's leg. All characters in the 彳 category are formed from 彳.

shuowen:1223.text: To ascend. Formed from 彳, with 㥁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1224.text: A footpath. Formed from 彳, with 巠 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1225.text: To come and go. Formed from 彳, with 复 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1226.text: To return. Formed from 彳 and 柔; 柔 also indicates the sound.

shuowen:1227.text: To walk directly. Formed from 彳, with 呈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1228.text: To go to. Formed from 彳, with 㞷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1229.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 彳, with 瞿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1230.text: To go, with something added. Formed from 彳, with 皮 indicating the sound. [The gloss is uncertain.]

shuowen:1231.text: To go around or follow. Formed from 彳, with 敫 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1232.text: To walk in accordance with a course. Formed from 彳, with 盾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1233.text: To walk hurriedly. Formed from 彳, with 及 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1234.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 彳, with 歰 indicating the sound. Another explanation: this is the same as 馺.

shuowen:1235.text: To travel secretly. Formed from 彳, with 𢼸 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Bai Gong's followers concealed him.”

shuowen:1236.text: 徥徥: a manner of walking. Formed from 彳, with 是 indicating the sound. The Erya says: “徥 means a rule or model.”

shuowen:1237.text: To walk calmly. Formed from 彳, with 余 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1238.text: To travel smoothly and easily. Formed from 彳, with 夷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1239.text: To send or employ. Formed from 彳, with 䛣 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1240.text: To send or employ. Formed from 彳, with 夆 indicating the sound. Read like 螽.

shuowen:1241.text: Tracks. Formed from 彳, with 戔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1242.text: To walk alongside. Formed from 彳, with 㫄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1243.text: To wait. Formed from 彳, with 奚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1244.text: To wait. Formed from 彳, with 寺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1245.text: To walk calmly or on level ground, in the repeated expression 㣙㣙. Formed from 彳, with 由 indicating the sound. [Duan identifies this as an interpretation of an obscure reduplicated form.]

shuowen:1246.text: To go all around. Formed from 彳, with 扁 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1247.text: To arrive. Formed from 彳, with 叚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1248.text: To retreat. Another explanation: to walk slowly. Formed from 彳, 日 and 夊.

shuowen:1249.text: Late or behind. Formed from 彳, 幺 and 夊, expressing being behind.

shuowen:1250.text: Long-lasting. Formed from 彳, with 犀 indicating the sound. Read like 遲.

shuowen:1251.text: Not to obey or follow. Another explanation: difficulty in walking; another: perverse. Formed from 彳, with 𥃩 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1252.text: To follow one another's tracks. Formed from 彳, with 重 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1253.text: To gain something in traveling. Formed from 彳, with 㝵 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1254.text: To cross water on a line of stepping-stones, lifting one’s legs to step over. Formed from 彳, with 奇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1255.text: To make a circuit of a military formation displaying or proclaiming an execution or order. Formed from 彳, with 勻 indicating the sound. The Methods of Sima says: “Execute and display it to the troops.”

shuowen:1256.text: To distribute evenly. Formed from 彳, with 聿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1257.text: To drive horses. Formed from 彳 and 卸.

shuowen:1258.text: To halt one's steps. Formed from reversed 彳. Read like 畜.

shuowen:1259.text: A long stride. Formed by extending 彳. All characters in the 廴 category are formed from 廴.

shuowen:1260.text: The center of the court. Formed from 廴, with 壬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1261.text: To walk. Formed from 廴, with 正 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1262.text: To establish the court's regulations. Formed from 聿 and 廴.

shuowen:1263.text: A calm gait, 㢟㢟. Formed from 廴 and 止. All characters in the 㢟 category are formed from 㢟.

shuowen:1264.text: A long stride. Formed from 㢟, with 丿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1265.text: A person's walking and hastening. Formed from 彳 and 亍. All characters in the 行 category are formed from 行.

shuowen:1266.text: A road within a settlement. Formed from 行, with 术 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1267.text: A road communicating in four directions. Formed from 行, with 圭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1268.text: A route reaching in four directions is called 衢. Formed from 行, with 瞿 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1269.text: A through road. Formed from 行, with 童 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Reaching the thoroughfare, he struck him with a dagger-axe.”

shuowen:1270.text: A street that passes through. Formed from 行, with 同 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1271.text: Tracks. Formed from 行, with 戔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1272.text: A manner of walking. Formed from 行, with 吾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1273.text: The appearance of walking joyfully. Formed from 行, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1274.text: To walk while selling. Formed from 行 and 言.

shuowen:1275.text: To lead and guard. Formed from 行, with 率 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1276.text: To stand guard. Formed from 韋 and 帀, and from 行; 行 represents the ranks of guards.

shuowen:1277.text: Bones in the mouth's gums. It depicts teeth in a mouth, with 止 indicating the sound. All characters in the 齒 category are formed from 齒.

shuowen:1278.text: The bases of the teeth, gums. Formed from 齒, with 斤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1279.text: To shed the milk teeth. Boys grow teeth at eight months and shed them at eight years; girls grow them at seven months and shed them at seven years. Formed from 齒 and 七.

shuowen:1280.text: Teeth meeting one another. Another explanation: to bite. Formed from 齒, with 責 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Fair-skinned and with meeting teeth.”

shuowen:1281.text: Teeth that are uneven or set against one another; another explanation is the appearance of bared teeth. Formed from 齒, with an abbreviated 柴 indicating the sound. Read like 柴. [Duan proposes 齘 in place of transmitted 齗.]

shuowen:1282.text: Teeth grinding against one another. Formed from 齒, with 介 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1283.text: The mouth open and teeth visible. Formed from 齒, with 只 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1284.text: Uneven teeth. Formed from 齒, with 兼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1285.text: Teeth pressed or crowded together, or biting. Another explanation concerns a hard object in a horse’s mouth. Formed from 齒, with 芻 indicating the sound. [The transmitted clause 馬口中糜 is disputed.]

shuowen:1286.text: Teeth not straight. Formed from 齒, with 禺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1287.text: Irregular teeth, 齬齒. Formed from 齒, with 虘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1288.text: Irregular teeth, 齵. Formed from 齒, with 取 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1289.text: Teeth of uneven lengths. Formed from 齒, with 差 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1290.text: The appearance of displaced, uneven teeth. Formed from 齒, with 佐 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Zheng had Zi 𪘓.”

shuowen:1291.text: Missing teeth. Another explanation: crooked teeth. Formed from 齒, with 𢍏 indicating the sound. Read like 權.

shuowen:1292.text: Without teeth. Formed from 齒, with 軍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1293.text: Missing teeth. Formed from 齒, with 獻 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1294.text: Swollen gums. Formed from 齒, with 巨 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1295.text: An old person's teeth. Formed from 齒, with 兒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1296.text: To bite. Formed from 齒, with 奇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1297.text: To bite with the teeth. Formed from 齒, with 出 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1298.text: To bite. Formed from 齒, with 㫺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1299.text: To bite. Formed from 齒, with 咸 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1300.text: To bite. Formed from 齒, with 𥃩 indicating the sound.
